hypotheses.justification: The goal `IsUnramifiedIn S ⊥` unfolds (Mathlib/RingTheory/Unramified/Locus.lean) to: for every prime P of S with `P.LiesOver ⊥`, `IsUnramifiedAt R P`. Take such a P. `Ideal.eq_bot_of_liesOver_bot` (GoingUp.lean:436) needs only `[Algebra.IsIntegral R S] [Nontrivial R] [IsDomain S]`, not injectivity, and gives P = ⊥. Then `LiesOver` says `(⊥ : Ideal S).under R = ⊥`. That comap is `RingHom.ker (algebraMap R S)`, so the kernel is ⊥ and `algebraMap R S` is injective. So `FaithfulSMul R S` follows from the other hypotheses inside the proof, through `faithfulSMul_iff_algebraMap_injective`. From there `Module.isTorsionFree_iff_algebraMap_injective` (Algebra/Basic.lean:485) or the instance `FaithfulSMul.to_isTorsionFree` gives `Module.IsTorsionFree R S`, and `isUnramifiedAt_bot` finishes as in the current proof. Degenerate case: if the map is not injective, no prime of S lies over ⊥ and the statement holds vacuously; the argument above covers this case. The other binders are not affected: `[IsDomain R]` can be dropped at the same time (see the other entry).

`Ideal R` and `IsUnramifiedIn` only need `CommRing R`, so the statement still elaborates without this binder. With `[FaithfulSMul R S]` and `[IsDomain S]` still present, `IsDomain.of_faithfulSMul R S` (Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Basic.lean:455) gives `IsDomain R`, and the proof then runs unchanged. It also works with `[FaithfulSMul R S]` removed as well. `R` is nontrivial because of `CharZero R`, so `Ideal.eq_bot_of_liesOver_bot` applies. For any prime P lying over ⊥ it gives P = ⊥, hence `ker (algebraMap R S) = ⊥`, so the map is injective. That gives `FaithfulSMul R S` and then `IsDomain R` locally, and `isUnramifiedAt_bot` finishes. So this binder and `[FaithfulSMul R S]` can each be removed, and also both together.
